sentences.zh: 然后这实际上是这个。

sentences.zh: 它在书里，不在电影里。

sentences.en: We are told how restless, power-hungry individuals within the government, aided by the massive organs of commerce, propelled the campaign of the ambitious Senator Palpatine,
sentences.zh: 我们被告知政府内部那些不安分、渴望权力的个人，在庞大的商业机构的帮助下，推动了野心勃勃的帕尔帕廷参议员的竞选活动，

sentences.en: who promised to reunite the disaffected among the people and to restore the remembered glory of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 他承诺重新团结人民中不满的人，并恢复共和国被遗忘的荣耀。

sentences.en: And so he surrounds himself, as it says, by boot lickers.
sentences.zh: 所以正如书中所说，他身边围绕着一群阿谀奉承之徒。

sentences.en: So this is Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是尤利乌斯·凯撒。

sentences.en: Palpatine is Julius Caesar, basically.
sentences.zh: 帕尔帕廷基本上就是尤利乌斯·凯撒。

sentences.en: Well, is he Julius Caesar or is he Augustus, Tom?
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆，他到底是尤利乌斯·凯撒还是奥古斯都？

sentences.en: Well, he's then Augustus when he proclaims himself emperor, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，当他自封为皇帝时，他就是奥古斯都了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a kind of a blurring of very, very negative portrayals of Caesar and of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上模糊了凯撒和奥古斯都那些非常、非常负面的形象。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think what's fascinating about this, what I find interesting about this is all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我觉得关于这一点，最让我着迷、最让我感兴趣的正是所有这些内容。

sentences.en: I'm sure Alan Dean Foster and George Lucas didn't think very much about it.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定艾伦·迪恩·福斯特和乔治·卢卡斯并没有过多地考虑这些。

sentences.en: I'm sure this wasn't conscious.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定这并非有意为之。

sentences.en: But that idea that the whole enterprise was destroyed from within, it couldn't be destroyed from without, it was destroyed from within.
sentences.zh: 但那种整个事业从内部瓦解的观念——它无法从外部被摧毁，而是从内部瓦解的。

sentences.en: And it was destroyed by people hungry for power, by boot lickers, and the organs of commerce, and all of this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 它被那些渴望权力的人、阿谀奉承之徒、商业机构以及所有这类东西所摧毁。

sentences.en: I think that's quite Gabonian.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有吉本的风格。

sentences.en: Well, it's 18th century American specifically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这具体是18世纪美国的风格。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because America is founded with this idea that it's a republic.
sentences.zh: 因为美国建立的初衷就是它是一个共和国。

sentences.en: Benjamin Franklin famously says it will be a republic if you can keep it.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林曾有名言：如果你能守护住它，它就是一个共和国。

sentences.en: And that anxiety that the republic might collapse and be replaced by an autocracy as Rome had been, and the American Republic is founded on the Roman Republic,
sentences.zh: 那种担心共和国可能会崩溃并被独裁统治所取代的焦虑，正如罗马曾经发生的那样，而美利坚共和国正是建立在罗马共和国的基础之上的，

sentences.en: I don't know the degree to which this is something that American students study in their history classes.
sentences.zh: 我不知道美国学生在历史课上学习这些内容的程度如何。

sentences.en: But it's kind of in the air.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎是一种普遍的氛围。

sentences.en: The fact that the visuals of the American Republic are so Roman means that that has always been an anxiety.
sentences.zh: 美利坚共和国的视觉形象如此具有罗马风格，这意味着这种焦虑一直存在。

sentences.en: Well, that anxiety, that fear of ambition, corruption, I mean, the mention of commerce and wealth, the idea of fear of luxury, those are very 18th century ideas, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那种焦虑，那种对野心、腐败的恐惧，我是说，提到商业和财富，对奢靡的恐惧，这些都是非常18世纪的思想，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they were very popular on both sides of the Atlantic in the political classes.
sentences.zh: 而且它们在大西洋两岸的政治阶层中都非常流行。

sentences.en: And so Gibbon, when he wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 所以吉本在撰写《罗马帝国衰亡史》时，

sentences.en: he moved in circles where people were dissing luxury and dissing ambition and corruption all the time.
sentences.zh: 他所处的圈子里的人一直在抨击奢靡、抨击野心和腐败。

sentences.en: And that sort of idea that great empires or great republics are undermined by the decadence
sentences.zh: 那种伟大的帝国或伟大的共和国会被统治阶级的颓废

sentences.en: and the degeneracy of their ruling classes, and then a strong man will arise to take power.
sentences.zh: 和堕落所削弱，然后强人就会崛起夺取权力的想法，

sentences.en: I mean, we all have that to some degree, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们多多少少都有这种想法，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we've absorbed it from popular culture.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们是从流行文化中吸收了这些观念。

sentences.en: Yes, but here's my question on that.
sentences.zh: 是的，但关于这一点我有个问题。

sentences.en: You're talking about how these books are written to tie in with the success of Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 你刚才谈到这些书是如何为了配合《星球大战》的成功而创作的。

sentences.en: And then in due course, George Lucas revisits the Star Wars universe and he comes up with three films that trace, you know, we discover who Darth Vader is, his backstory.
sentences.zh: 后来，乔治·卢卡斯重返《星球大战》宇宙，他创作了三部电影，追溯了——你知道，我们发现了达斯·维达是谁，他的背景故事。

sentences.en: And the backdrop to this is the implosion of the Republic and its replacement by an empire.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的背景是共和国的内爆及其被帝国所取代。

sentences.en: But presumably this was not in Lucas's mind when he first made Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 但据推测，卢卡斯在最初制作《星球大战》时并没有想到这一点。

sentences.en: It's this stuff that basically scholars and enthusiasts and geeks have been pouring over it and they have kind of drawn out these echoes.
sentences.zh: 正是这些东西，学者、爱好者和极客们一直在钻研，他们从中引申出了这些回响。

sentences.en: And is George Lucas then thinking, oh, wow, it's cleverer than I thought, or, you know, it has more echoes than I thought.
sentences.zh: 那么乔治·卢卡斯当时在想，哦，哇，这比我想象的更聪明，或者，你知道，它比我想象的有更多的回响。

sentences.en: And is he perhaps kind of responding to that?
sentences.zh: 他是否在某种程度上对此做出了回应？

sentences.en: I think possibly to some extent, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得在某种程度上是有可能的。

sentences.en: So Lucas said after Star Wars became successful, he said, this is actually episode four.
sentences.zh: 所以卢卡斯在《星球大战》大获成功后说，这实际上是第四部。

sentences.en: Now, it wasn't initially branded as episode four.
sentences.zh: 现在，它最初并没有被标记为第四部。

sentences.en: When you went to see Star Wars in 1977, it didn't say episode four.
sentences.zh: 当你1977年去看《星球大战》时，上面并没有写着第四部。

sentences.en: But when I went to see it, when it was re-released in 1980, when the Empire Strikes Back came out, they had put on the episode four branding.
sentences.zh: 但当我1980年重映时去看它，也就是《帝国反击战》上映时，他们加上了第四部的标签。

sentences.en: Because I can remember saying to my dad at the cinema, we've made a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得在电影院对我爸爸说，我们犯了一个严重的错误。

sentences.en: We've come late.
sentences.zh: 我们来晚了。

sentences.en: This is the fourth episode and we've missed the first three.
sentences.zh: 这是第四部，我们错过了前三部。

sentences.en: Whether he was really intending to make these prequels, I suspect probably not.
sentences.zh: 至于他是否真的打算制作这些前传，我怀疑可能没有。

sentences.en: He sort of would airily talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他只是轻描淡写地谈论过。

sentences.en: But again, it added to the sense of a deep history.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这增加了一种深厚历史感。

sentences.en: You know, actually you're coming in the middle of the story and people loved that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，实际上你是从故事中间切入的，人们很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: But those first three episodes, which I saw the first one, I thought it was so dull.
sentences.zh: 但那前三部，我看了第一部，我觉得太沉闷了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'd really rather have watched a film about trade negotiations in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我真的宁愿看一部关于布鲁塞尔贸易谈判的电影。

sentences.en: Well, you did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实看了。

sentences.en: You mean The Phantom Menace?
sentences.zh: 你是说《幽灵的威胁》？

sentences.en: The Phantom Menace is what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的就是《幽灵的威胁》。

sentences.en: So those three films, are the allusions to Rome clearer in those?
sentences.zh: 那么那三部电影中，对罗马的影射是否更清晰？

sentences.en: Are they more overt?
sentences.zh: 它们是否更直白？

sentences.en: They're much more overt.
sentences.zh: 它们要直白得多。

sentences.en: So not necessarily in The Phantom Menace.
sentences.zh: 所以不一定是在《幽灵的威胁》里。

sentences.en: I mean, these, by the way, for the avoidance of doubt, some of our listeners may like these filMs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，顺便说一句，为了避免疑义，我们的一些听众可能喜欢这些电影。

sentences.en: I have to be honest and say, although I love Star Wars, I absolutely loathe these filMs.
sentences.zh: 我必须诚实地说，虽然我喜欢《星球大战》，但我绝对讨厌这些电影。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's by the by.
sentences.zh: 总之，那是题外话。

sentences.en: They are more overt.
sentences.zh: 它们确实更直白。

sentences.en: So the story, the theme is the emergence of this Elber of Palpatine.
sentences.zh: 所以故事的主题是帕尔帕廷这个埃尔伯（Elber）的崛起。

sentences.en: I think what made it so disappointing for people of my age is that we had built up, we had our own private versions, you know, as people tend to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为让我们这一代人感到失望的是，我们已经建立了自己的私人版本，你知道，正如人们倾向于做的那样。

sentences.en: Like people did with the fall of Numenor in The Lord of the Rings, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像人们在《指环王》中对待努门诺尔的陷落一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We had our own vision of what this would have looked like.
sentences.zh: 我们有自己对这一切样子的设想。

sentences.en: And then when you discover it's sort of computer generated Jar Jar Binks, aliens and whatever, it's just so depressing.
sentences.zh: 然后当你发现它只是电脑生成的加·加·宾克斯、外星人什么的，真是太令人沮丧了。

sentences.en: Anyway, the one thing that is quite interesting is the emergence of this guy, Palpatine.
sentences.zh: 总之，有一点很有趣，那就是帕尔帕廷这个家伙的崛起。

sentences.en: He has secretly generated, Tom, all these sort of civil wars and separatist movements in order to be given emergency powers to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他暗中制造了所有这些内战和分裂运动，以便被授予紧急权力来处理它们。

sentences.en: And so he's given these emergency powers in the film Attack of the Clones.
sentences.zh: 所以他在电影《克隆人的进攻》中被授予了这些紧急权力。

sentences.en: I think Augustus is the better comparison than Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥古斯都比尤利乌斯·凯撒更适合作为比较对象。

sentences.en: He is given by the Senate these powers.
sentences.zh: 他被元老院授予了这些权力。

sentences.en: And he says to them, it is with great reluctance that I've agreed to this calling.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，我怀着极大的不情愿接受了这个使命。

sentences.en: I love democracy.
sentences.zh: 我热爱民主。

sentences.en: I love the Republic.
sentences.zh: 我热爱共和国。

sentences.en: Once this crisis has abated, I will lay down the powers you have given me.
sentences.zh: 一旦这场危机平息，我将交出你们赋予我的权力。

sentences.en: Of course, that is a Roman idea that someone will be awarded the powers of a dictator and then will surrender them.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一个罗马式的观念，即某人被授予独裁者的权力，然后又会交还它们。

sentences.en: And then in the final film of that prequel trilogy, Revenge of the Sith, he orchestrates a series of prescriptions, like the prescriptions that claim the life of Cicero,
sentences.zh: 然后在前传三部曲的最后一部《西斯的复仇》中，他策划了一系列公敌名单，就像那些导致西塞罗丧命的名单一样，

sentences.en: the prescriptions of Antony and Octavian.
sentences.zh: 安东尼和屋大维的名单。

sentences.en: And again, you think here this is a deliberate echo, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这又是一个刻意的回响吗？

sentences.en: I don't know how deliberate it is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这有多刻意。

sentences.en: There's also something in Light of the Long Knives about it, I guess, a sort of internal purge, the massacre of the Jedi Knights.
sentences.zh: 我想这其中也有点“长刀之夜”的影子，一种内部清洗，对绝地武士的大屠杀。

sentences.en: And then there's this scene, which is often sort of mocked on social media, when he's surrounded by kind of gibbering aliens and flying saucers.
sentences.zh: 然后是那个在社交媒体上经常被嘲笑的场景，他被一群叽叽喳喳的外星人和飞碟包围着。

sentences.en: And he says, in order to ensure our security and continuing stability, the Republic will be reorganized into the first galactic empire for a safe and secure society.
sentences.zh: 他说，为了确保我们的安全和持续的稳定，共和国将被改组为第一个银河帝国，以建立一个安全稳固的社会。

sentences.en: And Natalie Bortman's character, Queen Amidala, who is Luke and Leia's mother, she says very earnestly, So this is how liberty dies, with thunderous applause.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉·波特曼饰演的角色，阿米达拉女王，也就是卢克和莱娅的母亲，她非常诚恳地说：这就是自由死亡的方式，伴随着雷鸣般的掌声。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she is the Cicero of the Star Wars world.
sentences.zh: 所以她是《星球大战》世界的西塞罗。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So again, this is Rome in the era of Augustus and Tiberius or whatever, that the Senate has basically, in its sort of supine way,
sentences.zh: 所以这又是奥古斯都和提比略时代的罗马，元老院基本上以一种顺从的方式，

sentences.en: is handing over power to a power-hungry, malevolent character who affects this modesty, as of course Augustus did, but in reality is more ruthless than anybody.
sentences.zh: 将权力移交给了一个渴望权力、心怀叵测的角色，他装出谦逊的样子，正如奥古斯都当然做过的那样，但实际上比任何人都更冷酷无情。

sentences.en: Now, there's an Australian classical scholar called Michael Charles, who wrote an article about this in the journal,
sentences.zh: 现在，有一位名叫迈克尔·查尔斯的澳大利亚古典学者，他在期刊上写了一篇关于此的文章，

sentences.en: Classical World, Remembering and Restoring the Republic.
sentences.zh: 《古典世界》，《铭记与恢复共和国》。

sentences.en: And he says, one of the funny things about this, he says, and again, this is completely unconscious, I think,
sentences.zh: 他说，关于这一点有趣的事情之一是——我认为这完全是无意识的——

sentences.en: is that in Rome, people who criticized, you know, people who were ambivalent about the rise of Julius Caesar,
sentences.zh: 在罗马，那些批评——你知道，那些对尤利乌斯·凯撒的崛起持矛盾态度的人，

sentences.en: most obviously, and then I suppose Augustus, they were the patrician elite, weren't they, Tom?
sentences.zh: 最明显的是，我想还有奥古斯都，他们是贵族精英，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: They were, what do you call them, the bonnie?
sentences.zh: 他们是，你怎么称呼他们，邦尼（boni）？

sentences.en: Yeah, the optimates.
sentences.zh: 是的，贵族派（optimates）。

sentences.en: The good guys.
sentences.zh: 好人。

sentences.en: These are the people who look back, you know, who are upholders of tradition, who identify themselves with all that is best in Roman tradition, and who have to be incredibly rich.
sentences.zh: 这些人回顾过去，你知道，他们是传统的捍卫者，他们将自己与罗马传统中所有最美好的事物联系在一起，而且他们必须非常有钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the sense is, in the Star Wars universe, that all the defenders of the Republic are very, very posh.
sentences.zh: 而在《星球大战》宇宙中，给人的感觉是所有共和国的捍卫者都非常、非常时髦。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And rich.
sentences.zh: 而且富有。

sentences.en: I mean, they're literally princesses.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们简直就是公主。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And queens.
sentences.zh: 还有女王。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the person who says that line about liberty dying is Queen Amidala.
sentences.zh: 所以说出那句关于自由死亡台词的人是阿米达拉女王。

sentences.en: Her daughter is Princess Leia, and Princess Leia is the person who carries the torch of kind of republicanism.
sentences.zh: 她的女儿是莱娅公主，而莱娅公主是那个传承共和主义火炬的人。

sentences.en: Well, this will be familiar to people who may not have read books on Roman history, but have seen Gladiator, where in Gladiator you have the evil emperor, Commodus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对于那些可能没读过罗马历史书籍但看过《角斗士》的人来说会很熟悉，在《角斗士》中你有邪恶的皇帝康茂德。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The freedom fighters, and indeed the Christians, because the Jedi could be, you know,
sentences.zh: 自由战士，实际上还有基督徒，因为绝地武士可能，你知道，

sentences.en: there are kind of echoes of the way that early Christians play the role in Quo Vadis or Demetrius and the Gladiators, things like that.
sentences.zh: 早期基督徒在《暴君焚城录》或《德米特里与角斗士》等影片中扮演的角色有一些回响。

sentences.en: I think that's totally right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得这完全正确。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's a scholar who has written lots about this, who agrees with you, called Martin Winkler.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一位写过很多关于此的学者，他同意你的观点，名叫马丁·温克勒。

sentences.en: That's tremendous to know.
sentences.zh: 知道这一点真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And he has pointed out that Alec Guinness, who plays Ben Kenobi, Obi-Wan Kenobi, he would have been well known to American audiences for a whole host of roles.
sentences.zh: 他指出，饰演本·肯诺比（欧比旺·肯诺比）的亚历克·吉尼斯，对美国观众来说，他因扮演过许多角色而广为人知。

sentences.en: But one of them was playing Marcus Aurelius.
sentences.zh: 但其中之一就是扮演马可·奥勒留。

sentences.en: Oh, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: In the film The Fall of the Roman Empire in 1964.
sentences.zh: 在1964年的电影《罗马帝国沦亡录》中。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: The film that is the direct model for Gladiator.
sentences.zh: 那部电影是《角斗士》的直接蓝本。

sentences.en: I mean, Gladiator is really a remake of The Fall of the Roman Empire.

sentences.en: So it opens with someone arriving in the planet of Trantor.
sentences.zh: 故事开头是有人抵达了川陀星。

sentences.en: And so the opening, there were nearly 25 million inhabited planets in the galaxy then and not one but owed allegiance to the empire whose seat was on Trantor.
sentences.zh: 开头写道：当时银河系有近2500万个有人居住的行星，每一个都效忠于以川陀为中心的帝国。

sentences.en: Or it was the last half century in which that could be said.
sentences.zh: 或者说，这是能这样说的最后半个世纪。

sentences.en: So this is the equivalent of someone arriving in Rome in 400.
sentences.zh: 所以这相当于有人在400年抵达罗马。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Or is it a sort of a veiled reference to that bit in Gibbon when Gibbon says, you know, if you had to pick an age, you would have picked the age of the Antonines or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 或者这是否是对吉本那段话的隐晦引用？吉本说，如果你必须选择一个时代，你会选择安敦尼时代之类的。

sentences.en: But that's several centuries before, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那是几个世纪前的事了，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is, I mean, the decline is about to happen.
sentences.zh: 我是说，衰亡即将发生。

sentences.en: Okay, right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，没错。

sentences.en: You know, it's directly about to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它直接就要发生了。

sentences.en: And the parabola of Asimov's narrative directly follows that of Gibbon.
sentences.zh: 阿西莫夫叙事的抛物线直接遵循了吉本的轨迹。

sentences.en: So you have scenes in which imperial plenipotentiaries visit outposts of the empire for the very last time.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有帝国全权代表最后一次访问帝国边境的场景。

sentences.en: You get kind of interstellar equivalents of the barbarian kingdoms sprouting up on, you know, planets that the empire has abandoned.
sentences.zh: 你会看到星际版的蛮族王国在帝国遗弃的行星上涌现。

sentences.en: You have a chapter in which the empire, a bit like Justinian reinvading Italy, tries to kind of reconstitute the empire.
sentences.zh: 你有一章写帝国试图重建，有点像查士丁尼重新征服意大利。

sentences.en: But the foundation itself, which gives its name to the series of novels, is something that has been founded.
sentences.zh: 但“基地”本身，也就是这个系列小说的名字，是某样被建立起来的东西。

sentences.en: It's a foundation by a psycho historian, a guy called Harry Seldon.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由心理史学家哈里·谢顿建立的基地。

sentences.en: And he's a mathematician who has applied his kind of crunching of data to the past and has drawn up rules of history.
sentences.zh: 他是一位数学家，将他的数据处理应用到了过去，并制定了历史规律。

sentences.en: So by looking to the past, he's been able to work out the future.
sentences.zh: 所以通过审视过去，他能够推算出未来。

sentences.en: And so he can tell that the empire is going to collapse.
sentences.zh: 因此他能断定帝国即将崩溃。

sentences.en: And he kind of plants the foundation to serve as a beacon of light amid the gathering darkness that he knows is going to come.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上奠定了基础，要在自己预见的黑暗降临之际，充当一座指路明灯。

sentences.en: So it's as though he has read his Gibbon and he thinks this is going to happen again, effectively.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是他读过吉本的著作，认为这一切实际上会重演。

sentences.en: Yes, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: And so the whole series of novels revolves around the fact that there are kind of what are called Selden events,
sentences.zh: 所以整个系列小说都围绕着一种被称为“谢顿危机”的事件展开，

sentences.en: where some catastrophic thing that most people couldn't have seen.
sentences.zh: 即大多数人无法预见的灾难性事件。

sentences.en: But because he can, he's a psycho historian, he's been able to work it out.
sentences.zh: 但因为他能预见，他是一位心理史学家，所以他能够推算出来。

sentences.en: He knows what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 他知道将会发生什么。

sentences.en: And actually, I think this is a trend that's particularly popular in American universities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这在当今美国大学里是一个特别流行的趋势。

sentences.en: There are historians who are very into the idea that you can kind of draw immutable lessons.
sentences.zh: 有些历史学家非常热衷于那种可以总结出永恒教训的观点。

sentences.en: So I guess the Thucydides trap would be the classic example.
sentences.zh: 我想“修昔底德陷阱”就是一个典型的例子。

sentences.en: American sort of military historians love to talk about that, don't they?
sentences.zh: 美国的军事历史学家很喜欢谈论这个，不是吗？

sentences.en: Policymakers.
sentences.zh: 政策制定者也是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is the idea that a settled power will become the rival of a rising power.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的守成大国将成为崛起大国竞争对手的观点。

sentences.en: So Sparta goes to war with Athens.
sentences.zh: 所以斯巴达与雅典开战。

sentences.en: Britain goes to war with Germany.
sentences.zh: 英国与德国开战。

sentences.en: It's much applied now with regard to America and China.
sentences.zh: 现在这套理论被广泛应用于美国和中国的问题上。

sentences.en: And really, this is an idea.
sentences.zh: 说真的，这确实是一个观点。

sentences.en: This idea that you can have applied history is something that has been very popular in the United States throughout the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这种“应用历史学”的理念在整个20世纪的美国都非常流行。

sentences.en: And Asimov is clearly drawing on that idea, I think, with the foundation.
sentences.zh: 我想阿西莫夫在《基地》中显然借鉴了这一理念。

sentences.en: You know who would be a good, who's Harry Selden, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你知道谁会是合适的人选吗？谁是哈里·谢顿？

sentences.en: And Neil Ferguson.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·弗格森。

sentences.en: Neil Ferguson's all over this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·弗格森对这类事情非常热衷。

sentences.en: So Neil Ferguson did actually organise a conference on this very idea in Stanford, to which I was invited.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·弗格森确实在斯坦福大学组织过一场关于这个理念的会议，我也受邀参加了。

sentences.en: Tom, oh my word.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，天哪。

sentences.en: One of 19 men and one woman.
sentences.zh: 那是19名男性和1名女性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There was much uproar about this.
sentences.zh: 当时引起了很大的轰动。

sentences.zh: 我记得那被称为“香肠派对”。

sentences.en: How did that woman get in?
sentences.zh: 那位女士是怎么混进去的？

sentences.en: Unbelievable scenes.
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议。

sentences.en: But you know, it was in California.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，那是在加州。

sentences.en: I think the beast from the east was sweeping in over Britain.
sentences.zh: 当时“东方野兽”寒潮正席卷英国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I went and enjoyed the sun.
sentences.zh: 我去了那里，享受了阳光。

sentences.zh: 你对未来做了什么预测？

sentences.zh: 我做了一个关于“不死罗马”的演讲。

sentences.en: I did it on looking at how ideas of Rome motivated Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 我研究了罗马的观念是如何激励弗拉基米尔·普京的。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天呐。

sentences.en: We ended up talking about it in one of the episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们在其中一集里讨论过这个话题。

sentences.en: You know, never let anything go to waste.
sentences.zh: 你知道，永远不要浪费任何东西。

sentences.en: Anyway, this is still quite a current idea.
sentences.zh: 总之，这仍然是一个非常热门的话题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But in the context of this idea that Gibbon articulates, that the fall of the Roman Empire is the greatest, perhaps, and most awful scene in the history of mankind,
sentences.zh: 但在吉本所阐述的那个背景下，即罗马帝国的衰亡或许是人类历史上最伟大、最可怕的场景，

sentences.en: he famously says.
sentences.zh: 他曾有名言。

sentences.en: There is a great twist in the second novel, which is that Harry Selden's reading of history turns out to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 第二部小说中有一个巨大的转折，那就是哈里·谢顿的历史推演出了错。

sentences.en: An event happens that he couldn't have foreseen.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件他无法预见的事情。

sentences.en: And this is the emergence of a character called the Mule, who is a mutant telepath.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个名叫“骡”的角色的出现，他是一个变异的心灵感应者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he can read and manipulate the emotions of other people.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以读取并操纵他人的情绪。

sentences.en: And he ends up conquering the galaxy and conquering the foundation.
sentences.zh: 最终他征服了银河系，也征服了基地。

sentences.en: He has not been predicted.
sentences.zh: 他没有被预测到。

sentences.en: And I think that this is pretty clearly an echo of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 我认为这显然是在呼应穆罕默德。

sentences.en: It's a fairly hostile portrayal of Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当敌意的穆罕默德形象刻画。

sentences.en: The Mule is a kind of, he's an arrogant conqueror.
sentences.zh: “骡”是一个傲慢的征服者。

sentences.en: But I think it is an interesting twist because essentially what Asimov is saying there is that the emergence of Islam is a kind of, you know, a lightning bolt from the blue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个有趣的转折，因为阿西莫夫本质上是在说，伊斯兰教的兴起就像是一道晴天霹雳。

sentences.en: It couldn't have been anticipated or foreseen.
sentences.zh: 它是无法被预料或预见的。

sentences.en: It's something so startling and unexpected that even the most highly advanced psycho historians could not have anticipated it.
sentences.zh: 它是如此令人震惊和出乎意料，以至于即使是最先进的心理史学家也无法预见。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is buying into the traditional Islamic narrative that Islam emerges because it is a revelation of God rather than emerging, as I think it probably did,
sentences.zh: 当然，这迎合了传统的伊斯兰叙事，即伊斯兰教的出现是因为它是上帝的启示，而不是像我认为的那样，

sentences.en: in quite a predictable way from the kind of the melange of opinions and religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 以一种相当可预测的方式，从各种观点和宗教信仰的混合中产生。

sentences.en: So if Harry Selden is a psycho, what is he, a psycho historian?
sentences.zh: 那么如果哈里·谢顿是心理学家，他是什么，心理史学家？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If he'd been trained in the sort of 1970s and 1980s by sort of a Patricia Croner figure, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，如果他是在七八十年代受过帕特里夏·克罗内那种人物的训练，

sentences.en: Yeah, he might have seen it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他可能就看出来了。

sentences.en: He would have seen it coming because he would have said Islam emerged out of the superpower conflicts in Arabia between the Romans and the Persians and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他会预见到它的到来，因为他会说伊斯兰教是从阿拉伯半岛罗马人和波斯人之间的超级大国冲突中产生的。

sentences.en: But I guess what Asimov is reflecting is the orthodox historiography about the rise of Islam and the sort of 7th century at the time he was writing in the 1950s, right?
sentences.zh: 但我猜阿西莫夫反映的是他写作的50年代时，关于伊斯兰教兴起和7世纪的正统史学观点，对吧？

sentences.en: As is another equally celebrated work of science fiction, a series of novels like Foundation that, again, have inspired, not TV in this case,
sentences.zh: 还有另一部同样著名的科幻作品，像《基地》一样的小说系列，同样激发了灵感，虽然这次不是电视剧，

sentences.en: but a couple of films so far that are out on release.
sentences.zh: 而是目前已经上映的两部电影。

sentences.en: And that's Dune.
sentences.zh: 那就是《沙丘》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Dune was written in the 60s by a guy called Frank Herbert.
sentences.zh: 《沙丘》是60年代由弗兰克·赫伯特写的。

sentences.en: And it's set on an inhospitable desert, a bit like, what is it, Tatooine, is it?
sentences.zh: 故事发生在一个荒凉的沙漠星球上，有点像，是什么来着，塔图因？

sentences.en: In Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 在《星球大战》里。

sentences.en: Or Jakku.
sentences.zh: 或者贾库。

sentences.en: So this is Arrakis.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是厄拉科斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's full of giant kind of sandworms and things.
sentences.zh: 那里到处都是巨大的沙虫之类的东西。

sentences.en: But what Arrakis produces is a kind of weird thing called spice.
sentences.zh: 但厄拉科斯出产一种奇怪的东西，叫香料。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That effectively powers space travel.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是太空旅行的动力来源。

sentences.en: Which is also called melange, rather oddly.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，它也被称为“美琅脂”。

sentences.en: Or melange.
sentences.zh: 或者说美琅脂。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's, I mean, this is just before OPEC.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这正好是在欧佩克成立之前。

sentences.en: So it's pretty clear that this is spice in a way is oil.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这种香料在某种程度上就是石油。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think it is clearly also an echo of the idea that was very, very current when Herbert was writing this and which Patricia Croner delivered a kind of devastating rebuttal to.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这显然也呼应了赫伯特写作时非常流行的一种观点，而帕特里夏·克罗内对此进行了毁灭性的反驳。

sentences.en: The idea that Mecca had been a great center of the spice trade.
sentences.zh: 即麦加曾是香料贸易中心这一观点。

sentences.en: And that this is the context from which Mohammed emerges, that Mecca was this hugely significant center.
sentences.zh: 而这就是穆罕默德崛起的背景，即麦加是一个极其重要的中心。

sentences.en: I think it's absolutely clear that it wasn't at all.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全可以肯定事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And that this sense of Mecca as a center of spice trade is a kind of Orientalist fantasy that's projected onto the understanding of Islam by Western scholars who have this idea that anything Oriental must have to do with spice.
sentences.zh: 这种将麦加视为香料贸易中心的观念，是一种东方主义幻想，是西方学者投射到对伊斯兰教理解上的，因为他们认为任何东方事物都一定与香料有关。

sentences.en: And then it's turbocharged by the oil crisis.
sentences.zh: 然后石油危机又给这种观点加了把火。

sentences.en: Why does it matter in the history of Islam and the sort of collapse of the Roman authority in the Eastern Mediterranean?
sentences.zh: 为什么这在伊斯兰教历史和罗马帝国在东地中海权威的崩溃中很重要？

sentences.en: Why does it matter whether Mecca had spices or not?

sentences.zh: 我不认为这特别重要。

sentences.en: I mean, it matters very much to explaining the traditional accounts of Islam as history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对于解释伊斯兰教作为历史的传统叙述非常重要。

sentences.en: Because in the traditional accounts, Mecca is clearly a very significant settlement with all kinds of competing aristocracies.
sentences.zh: 因为在传统叙述中，麦加显然是一个非常重要的定居点，拥有各种相互竞争的贵族。

sentences.en: And historically, that doesn't seem to have been the case.
sentences.zh: 但在历史上，情况似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: There is no record of a Mecca that would correspond to a center that rich and that significant in any of the contemporary sources.
sentences.zh: 在任何同时代的文献中，都没有关于麦加作为一个如此富裕和重要的中心的记录。

sentences.en: But that idea of competing clans and aristocracies fighting for control of the spice trade, let's say.
sentences.zh: 但那种相互竞争的氏族和贵族为了争夺香料贸易控制权的想法，我们姑且这么说。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 希腊名字。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 我认为，这又是与伊斯兰历史的呼应。

sentences.zh: 因为保罗后来成为了穆阿迪布，在阿拉伯语中意为“老师”，尽管在《沙丘》中它实际上是指跳鼠。

sentences.en: So it's one of the animals of the desert.
sentences.zh: 所以它是沙漠中的一种动物。

sentences.en: And he goes on to kind of become a prophetic figure, a great religious leader.
sentences.zh: 他后来成为了一种预言式的人物，一位伟大的宗教领袖。

sentences.en: He launches this jihad, which ends up consuming the entire galactic empire, quite Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 他发动了圣战，最终吞噬了整个银河帝国，这很像《星球大战》。

sentences.en: And again, I think that this is consciously inspired by the way that Islam is a terminal event in the long run for the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为这是有意识地受到伊斯兰教作为罗马帝国长期终结事件这一方式的启发。
